key_insight: Microrollers slow down in confinement and can reverse direction as channels narrow, because far-field rotlet stress and near-field shear resistance compete differently under tight geometries.
engineering_relevance: The scaling framework can guide microchannel and biomedical device design for controlling particle transport, mixing, and targeted microroller motion under confinement.
method: Experiments in constricted, rectangular, and cylindrical microchannels
Numerical simulations of microroller dynamics under varying confinement
Force-free scaling analysis to link velocity to channel geometry
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the predicted confinement-dependent velocity trends agree well with both experiments and simulations.
watch_item: The scaling laws may depend on the specific particle shape, surface conditions, and channel geometry, so direct transfer to other setups should be validated.
paper_title: Dynamics of a microroller under confinement
